assessmentSummary.identity: Supine feet-on-wall 90/90 hip lift with heel pull, a small pelvic lift, gentle ball squeeze, right arm overhead, left hand controlling a personal balloon, comfortable nasal inhale, and slow resisted balloon exhale. The exact laterality, equipment, lift, and breath cycle are identity-bearing.
currentCardFindings: Boyle et al. directly describe the sequence as a clinical suggestion and theoretical rationale, not an outcome trial or universal treatment.
This is not the generic legacy Hip Reset source, which lacks the facts required to map to this action and remains quarantined.
The review-only difficulty proposal is 48 exercise complexity, 20 physical difficulty, and derived overall 48; equipment, laterality, lift, and resisted exhale drive complexity.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Use only when the exact hip-lift/ball/balloon coordination task is selected, equipment and hygiene pass, laterality is declared, direct sightline is available, and current symptoms permit. Passive reach, lateral-expansion breathing, no-balloon hip lift, mirrored arms, hip shift, Dead Bug, and Box Breath are distinct definitions or unresolved variants.

calibrationEvidence.basis: exact Boyle sequence plus heterogeneous breathing research and adjacent-card comparison
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: The exact source is a clinical suggestion; it does not establish treatment efficacy, universal safety, optimal dose, recovery, score, or progression order.

currentCardSnapshot.description: From a supine feet-on-wall 90/90 start, place a 4–6 inch ball between the knees, keep the right arm overhead, and hold the balloon with the left hand. Use a heel pull to establish a small posterior pelvic lift while maintaining ball pressure, then perform the declared nasal-inhale and balloon-exhale cycles without losing the lift, ball, wall, arm, or balloon seal contract. This exact asymmetric clinical-suggestion sequence is distinct from passive supported breathing with reach.

environment.changeRule: Changing arm laterality, removing the ball or balloon, adding a hip shift or hemibridge, changing pelvic-lift action, or using passive leg support changes the exact identity and requires separate review.

evidence.sourceTitle: The health effects of diaphragmatic breathing: A systematic review
claims: Diaphragmatic-breathing protocols, populations, outcomes, and reporting are highly heterogeneous, and no source assigns a Vortex difficulty score or participant classification.

evidence.sourceTitle: The health effects of diaphragmatic breathing: A systematic review
claims: Low external load does not mean zero exposure, while safety and adverse-event reporting in the breathing literature are incomplete.

Track valid, invalid, partial, assisted, and symptom-limited cycles; breath effort; position and equipment demand; prior trunk and respiratory work; duration; and recovery only as a conservative planning estimate.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period
evidence.sourcePublisher: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
claims: ACOG advises avoiding prolonged supine exercise after 20 weeks of pregnancy and individualizing activity; this general guidance is not clinical clearance for 90/90 Hip Lift with Ball and Balloon.

Require safe floor access, stable supports and equipment, comfortable unforced breathing, current symptom screening, accessible instruction, and a separately reviewed non-supine option when indicated.

evidence.sourceTitle: The health effects of diaphragmatic breathing: A systematic review
claims: The systematic review reports heterogeneous protocols and underreported safety, so absence of reported harm does not establish universal safety.

Do not force inhale, exhale, pressure, or retention. Stop for pain, dizziness, faintness, chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, panic, air hunger, neurologic signs, position or equipment failure, or inability to reset comfortably.

evidence.sourceTitle: How Breath-Control Can Change Your Life: A Systematic Review on Psycho-Physiological Correlates of Slow Breathing
claims: Slow-breathing studies use varied protocols and proposed mechanisms, so they do not prove one universal phase placement, autonomic reset, treatment effect, recovery acceleration, or sport transfer.

Use 90/90 Hip Lift with Ball and Balloon only for an observable low-load breath or coordination purpose, with exact identity, dose, cumulative exposure, duration, logistics, and substitution revalidation.
VA guidance presents supported position, comfortable nasal inhale, longer exhale, and gradual practice in plain language.
Athlete support must show the exact setup and action, expected low effort, self-checks, unexpected symptoms, stop signal, accessible alternatives, and safe exit without treatment claims.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Value of Blowing Up a Balloon
evidence.sourcePublisher: North American Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: The exact sequence exposes observable feet, heel pull, lift height, ball pressure, arm laterality, balloon seal, face and neck strain, and breath-cycle checkpoints.

FMS hands-on-ribs breathing has no heel pull, lift, ball, balloon, overhead arm, or asymmetric equipment handling.
Passive lateral expansion and bilateral reach are distinct cards; mirrored arms, no balloon, hip shift, hemibridge, right-arm reach, or high bridge are not silently equivalent to this exact sequence.
